title: Sobriety Savings Run-Rate
dataSources: Alcohol drinks (`alcohol:drink`), vice logs (`vice:log`), hydration intake (`hydration:intake`), swear-jar entries (`swearjar:entry`).
app: Habit and sobriety trackers, alcohol-unit and hydration logs, vaping/smoking cessation apps, and a smart swear jar — sent to Splunk HEC via scripted inputs and MQTT.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=vice:log saved_amount=*
| bin _time span=1w
| stats sum(saved_amount) as saved by _time
| eventstats avg(saved) as avg_weekly_saved
| eval annualised=round(avg_weekly_saved*52,2)
| sort - _time
description: Turns each cut-back decision into a visible savings run-rate instead of a vague nice idea.
value: Money saved is a powerful reinforcement loop for habits that otherwise feel like only deprivation.
implementation: Record the estimated amount saved for skipped vice events; chart weekly totals and the annualised savings trend.
visualization: Weekly savings chart with an annualised run-rate tile.
grandmaExplanation: It checks how much money cutting back is really saving you, which makes progress feel concrete and worth keeping.
